record.context_brief: Combinatorial consequences of extremal factorization ranks
record.original_question: Let G be a graph with average mixing matrix \hat{M}. In the extremal cases where either the non-negative rank of \hat{M} or the completely positive semidefinite rank of \hat{M} attains its boundary behavior, determine what combinatorial consequences for G can be deduced from those extremal rank values.

artifact.category_tag: average mixing matrix in quantum walks
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A$, and let $A = \sum_{r} \lambda_r E_r$ be its spectral decomposition, where the $E_r$ are the orthogonal projections onto the eigenspaces of $A$. The continuous-time quantum walk on $G$ is governed by the unitary $U(t) = e^{itA}$, and its average mixing matrix is defined by
$$\hat{M} = \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T}\int_0^T U(t) \circ \overline{U(t)}\, dt = \sum_{r} E_r \circ E_r,$$
where $\circ$ denotes the entrywise (Schur) product. The matrix $\hat{M}$ is doubly stochastic, symmetric, positive semidefinite, and entrywise non-negative.

Recall the following two notions of rank for non-negative / completely positive semidefinite matrices:
\begin{itemize}
\item The non-negative rank $\mathrm{rank}_+(M)$ of an entrywise non-negative $n \times n$ matrix $M$ is the least integer $k$ for which there exist non-negative vectors $u_1,\dots,u_k,v_1,\dots,v_k \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^n$ such that $M = \sum_{i=1}^k u_i v_i^{\top}$.
\item A symmetric $n \times n$ matrix $M$ is completely positive semidefinite (cpsd) if there exist Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices $P_1,\dots,P_n \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$ with $M_{ij} = \mathrm{Tr}(P_i P_j)$ for all $i,j$. The cpsd-rank $\mathrm{rank}_{\mathrm{cpsd}}(M)$ is the smallest such $d$.
\end{itemize}

Both $\mathrm{rank}_+(\hat{M})$ and $\mathrm{rank}_{\mathrm{cpsd}}(\hat{M})$ are well defined and satisfy elementary bounds (for instance, $\mathrm{rank}(\hat{M}) \le \mathrm{rank}_+(\hat{M})$, and similar relations hold for the cpsd-rank).

Problem: Characterize the combinatorial structure of $G$ in the extremal cases for these ranks. Specifically:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Describe the graphs $G$ for which $\mathrm{rank}_+(\hat{M})$ attains its minimum or maximum possible value (relative to natural bounds in terms of $n$ and $\mathrm{rank}(\hat{M})$), and determine the combinatorial consequences (such as regularity, vertex-transitivity, presence of twins, equitable partitions, or spectral properties of $A$) implied by each extremal value.
\item Do the same for $\mathrm{rank}_{\mathrm{cpsd}}(\hat{M})$.
\end{enumerate>
artifact.status_search_result: No publication was found that resolves the combinatorial characterization of graphs whose average mixing matrix attains extremal non-negative or cpsd rank. Recent work studies the average mixing matrix and the cpsd-rank separately but does not address this extremal-rank question, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A New Perspective on the Average Mixing Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Average mixing matrix characterized as projection onto the commutant algebra of the adjacency matrix; connections to graph automorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature on the average mixing matrix studies its rank and combinatorial implications but does not resolve the extremal non-negative or cpsd rank case.

status_evidence.title: Completely positive semidefinite rank
status_evidence.snippet: No general upper bound is known on the cpsd-rank of a cpsd matrix; the notion is recent and many basic questions remain open.
status_evidence.claim: The cpsd-rank of arbitrary cpsd matrices is poorly understood, supporting that the question for average mixing matrices is open.

status_evidence.title: Matrices with high completely positive semidefinite rank
status_evidence.snippet: Studies extremal behavior of cpsd-rank for general matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Extremal cpsd-rank results for general matrices exist but are not specialized to average mixing matrices of graphs.
